newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GRABOPLAST STEALS THE SHOW ON BUDAPEST MKT.
newsitem.headline: GRABOPLAST STEALS THE SHOW ON BUDAPEST MKT.

text.p: Hungarian home products and textiles maker Graboplast rose in large block deals on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, while most heavyweight shares dropped on corrections, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 3632.24 points, down 2.56 points.
Spot share turnover amounted to 2.2 billion forints with Graboplast, which closed up 100 at 4,750 forints, accounting for 853.8 million forints.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) may have sold its shares in Graboplast in two block deals, dealers said.
The EBRD did not have any immediate comment.
Traders added that Hungary's privatisation scandal, which led to the dismissal of all the leading privatisation officials at the end of last week, had not affected the stock market.
"I think we can speak about a correction, which followed the record highs of the past two weeks," Tamas Revesz of Gog Securities told Reuters.
The price of OTP Bank moved erratically.

Dealers said Monday's speculative deals on London's SEAQ pushed OTP up and the Budapest bourse followed this movement but the stock could not keep the high opening level of 2,830 forints and closed at 2,760, down 10.

Drugs maker Richter continued to fall, weakened by the supply of employee shares which has been flowing onto the market for days, while large investors have been waiting for a still lower price, Revesz said.
